POLICY ECONOMIST · EMPIRICAL MACROECONOMICS
:::


I am a Research Economist at the Ministry of Finance of Hungary and a PhD Candidate in Economics at Corvinus University of Budapest. My work combines empirical macroeconomics, monetary policy, forecasting and econometric modelling to study how policy intervention and macro-financial shocks shape the economy.

## Selected research

::: {.research-grid}
::: {.research-card .featured}
::: {.card-kicker}
DISSERTATION · CHAPTER 1
:::

### Monetary Transmission in a Fragmented Uncertain World

How does uncertainty change the effectiveness of monetary policy? Evidence from Bayesian threshold VARs across 30 economies.

[Working paper ↗](papers/uncertainty_transmission.pdf){.card-link}
:::

::: {.research-card}
::: {.card-kicker}
PUBLISHED · 2026
:::

### Nonlinear Transmission of Monetary Policy and Housing Market Imbalances: Evidence From a Factor-Augmented Threshold VAR Analysis

Housing-market states alter the behaviour of monetary policy and modestly amplify the contraction in real and financial aggregates.

[Journal article ↗](https://doi.org/10.1111/manc.70034){.card-link}
:::

::: {.research-card}
::: {.card-kicker}
DISSERTATION · CHAPTER 3
:::

### A Distributional Perspective on Forward Guidance and Monetary Policy along the US Term Structure

Monetary policy and forward guidance shocks move not only the conditional mean of yields, but also their conditional volatility.

[Working paper ↗](papers/forwardguidance_volatility.pdf){.card-link}
:::

::: {.research-card}
::: {.card-kicker}
POLICY RESEARCH · EIB
:::

### How Does Grant Design Shape Investment, Output, and Productivity in Europe?

Evidence on how the design and allocation of investment grants influence macroeconomic outcomes across EU economies.

[Working paper ↗](papers/macrogrants.pdf){.card-link}
:::
:::
